context: An elderly couple reflects on a longtime friend's ways
purpose: Teach: かまわ/しゃべっ/とたん/行ない/疑わ/楽しま/好む/もて

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 田中さん、若い頃から誰彼かまわずしゃべっていたな。
lines.en: Tanaka sure could talk to anyone, even back when he was young.
lines.style: Gentle, nostalgic smile in the voice. Unhurried pace, the comfort of long memory. A quiet observation shared, not performed. Slight warmth on the name.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。会ったとたん、行ない丁寧で、私はすぐに好むようになったわ。
lines.en: Yes. The moment we met, his manners were so careful and considerate — I took to him right away.
lines.style: Soft but clear. A woman remembering something true about someone she valued. Pace slows on the middle clause, lingering. Closes with gentle finality, no question mark in her tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔は女性にもよくもてていた。本人は疑わずにいたが。
lines.en: He was popular with women too, back then. Though he never seemed to notice it himself.
lines.style: Amused at the memory, but not unkindly. Light, knowing tone. Pause before the final clause — a small acknowledgment of his innocence. Voice carries both fondness and gentle amusement.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 今は、奥様としっかり楽しまれているそうよ。
lines.en: Now I hear he and his wife really do enjoy life together.
lines.style: Pleased, almost satisfied. Warm approval in a simple statement. The slight lift of someone remarking on something turning out the way it should. Conversational but genuinely glad.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.style: Quiet, deliberate. A small nod in the voice. The period at the end is absolute — no more need be said. Peaceful, settled. This is his last word on a conversation well-closed.
